Configuration reference¶

The VisIVO Visual Analytics backend is configured through environment variables, read when the backend starts (a few are re-read on every request; those are marked). Set them in the shell that launches uvicorn, in the container’s environment, or in the environment: block of a compose file.

Every default below is the value in the backend code. Sizes are in bytes and times in seconds unless stated otherwise; 1 GiB is 1073741824 bytes. Boolean switches name the values they accept, because they are not all parsed the same way.

Variables marked secret hold credentials. Keep them out of shell history, scripts under version control and log files; prefer an env file readable only by the service account.

The variables used by the cluster launch scripts (VISIVO_PARTITION, VISIVO_TIME, VISIVO_SIF, VISIVO_GRES and the others read by scripts/launch_backend_slurm.sh) configure the job, not the backend, and are documented in Running the backend on a cluster.

Worker pool and admission¶

CPU-bound work runs in one process pool. Heavy tasks (moments, isosurfaces, PV slices, spectral fits) are throttled so that at least one worker stays free for interactive requests such as slice scrolling and probing; see Async patterns for the design.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_WORKERS

4

Number of worker processes in the pool. The default is a fixed 4, not derived from the CPU count.

VISIVO_HEAVY_SLOTS

max(1, VISIVO_WORKERS - 1)

Heavy tasks allowed to occupy the pool at once. Set it to VISIVO_WORKERS to give up the reserved interactive slot, or to 1 to serialise heavy work.

VISIVO_HEAVY_TIMEOUT_S

900

Wall-clock ceiling for one heavy task; beyond it the request answers HTTP 504 and its slot is released. 0 disables the ceiling. The worker process itself may still run to completion.

VISIVO_MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS

3

Compute tasks one session may run at once; further requests wait (see below) and then answer HTTP 429.

VISIVO_TASK_SLOT_WAIT_S

15

How long a request waits for a free per-session slot before answering 429. 0 refuses immediately.

VISIVO_MP_START_METHOD

spawn

Start method of the worker processes (spawn, fork or forkserver). spawn is required when workers use CUDA. An unknown value falls back to the platform default, with a warning.

VISIVO_GPU_ROUND_ROBIN

1

With 1, each worker is pinned to one GPU in turn (through CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES), taken from the inherited CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or, failing that, from nvidia-smi -L. Any other value turns pinning off.

VISIVO_PRODUCT_CACHE_ENTRIES

32

Capacity of the in-memory LRU cache of computed products (moment, isosurface, PV, line width). Identical recomputations are served from it.

Memory and full-resolution loading¶

The backend measures the memory it can use from the tightest of: the cgroup memory limit at each level of its own cgroup (cgroup v2 memory.max, else cgroup v1 memory.limit_in_bytes), the memory SLURM granted the job, and, when none of these exists, the host’s physical memory. The available memory is the headroom under those limits, or the host’s available memory.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_FULL_RES_THRESHOLD_BYTES

min(4 GiB, memory limit / 4)

File size at or above which the backend tells the client to open a cube as a preview only (recommended_load_mode = preview_only). The user can still load full resolution or crop explicitly. When set, the value is used as is, with no memory check.

VISIVO_CGROUP_ROOT

the process’s own cgroup

cgroup v2 directory to read the memory and CPU limits from. When set, cgroup v1 is not consulted. Useful when /proc/self/cgroup does not name the right group.

Moments and Dask¶

How a moment map is computed depends on the size of the selected channel range, channels × NAXIS1 × NAXIS2 × 4 bytes (float32):

  1. With VISIVO_DASK_MODE=auto (the default) and Dask installed, the moment is computed with chunked dask.array: always on the distributed cluster when VISIVO_DASK_SCHEDULER names a reachable one, otherwise with a local threaded scheduler once the range reaches VISIVO_DASK_MIN_BYTES. Blocks are read from disk on demand; each holds at most 64 channels and at most VISIVO_MOMENT_CHUNK_BYTES, and at least one channel.

  2. Otherwise the worker keeps the range in memory only when it is no larger than min(VISIVO_MOMENT_STREAM_BYTES, available memory / 12). The factor 12 covers the float64 temporaries of the reduction.

  3. A larger range is streamed from disk: M0, M1 and M2 in spectral slabs, M3 to M10 through the same chunked Dask path (if Dask is installed; without it they fall back to memory). Slabs are sized like the Dask blocks, by VISIVO_MOMENT_CHUNK_BYTES, with VISIVO_MOMENT_SLAB_CHANNELS as the cap on their channel count.

Moments that need the centroid first (M2 to M5) are computed in two passes over the data on both out-of-core paths, so memory stays bounded by one block.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_MOMENT_STREAM_BYTES

2 GiB

Ceiling of the channel range kept in memory; the effective threshold is the smaller of this and one twelfth of the available memory.

VISIVO_MOMENT_CHUNK_BYTES

64 MiB

Size of each streamed slab or Dask block, never less than one channel.

VISIVO_MOMENT_SLAB_CHANNELS

64

Upper limit on the channels in a streamed slab. It only caps the slab; the size comes from VISIVO_MOMENT_CHUNK_BYTES.

VISIVO_MOMENT_THREADS

0

Threads for the parallel moment kernels and the local Dask scheduler. 0 means min(4, CPU count).

VISIVO_DASK_MODE

auto

auto: distributed if a scheduler is set, else local threaded Dask for large ranges. off: never Dask. local: always local threaded Dask. distributed: only a cluster, else the plain worker.

VISIVO_DASK_MIN_BYTES

512 MiB

In auto mode, smallest range sent to the local threaded Dask path.

VISIVO_DASK_SCHEDULER

unset

Address of a dask.distributed scheduler (for example tcp://host:8786). When set, moments are computed on that cluster; its workers must see the same files.

Rendering¶

Remote 3-D views (Cube viewer) are rendered by the backend, each in a process of its own.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_RENDER_MAX_SESSIONS

8

Remote views accepted at once; beyond it a new view answers HTTP 503.

VISIVO_RENDER_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS

300

A view that receives no command for this long is closed.

VISIVO_RENDER_IN_PROCESS

unset

1 renders inside the backend’s own process instead of a child process (slower: rendering then competes with the process that serves the clients).

SRC node¶

Settings for a backend that runs as a node of the SKA Regional Centre network and is discovered by a SKAVA catalogue; see The backend as an SRC node and SKAVA discovery.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_NODE_CODE

unset

The node’s code in the catalogue, reported in /v1/node/status and in pushed telemetry.

VISIVO_NODE_GPU

unset

1/true/yes declares a GPU, 0/false/no declares none; unset reports “unknown”.

VISIVO_NODE_STATUS_PUBLIC

1

0/false/no makes /v1/node/status and the metrics require the backend token. /v1/ping always stays open. Re-read on every request.

VISIVO_VERSION

the application version

Version string reported in the node status.

VISIVO_DATA_ROOT

unset

A single directory that file:// access URLs from SKAVA and the SODA service may point into. Combined with VISIVO_DATA_ROOTS; either is enough.

VISIVO_SKAVA_TELEMETRY_URL

unset

Base URL (http or https) of the catalogue to push the node status to. Pushing is off unless this, the token and the node code are all set.

VISIVO_SKAVA_NODE_TOKEN

unset

Secret. This node’s telemetry token, issued by the catalogue’s operator.

VISIVO_SKAVA_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL

10

Seconds between pushed reports; at least 1.

Security, tokens and multi-user¶

See Sharing one backend between users for how these fit together.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_TOKEN

generated at startup

Secret. The primary (operator) token. When unset, a random token is generated, printed at startup and written to ~/.visivo_token (mode 600). Re-read on every request, so it can be rotated.

VISIVO_TOKENS

unset

Secret. Additional per-user tokens, comma- or whitespace-separated. More than one accepted token switches on multi-user mode. Re-read on every request.

VISIVO_DATA_ROOTS

unset

Directories (separated by : on Linux and macOS, ; on Windows) that path-based endpoints may read. Unset: unconfined with a single token, all path access denied in multi-user mode. Re-read on every request.

VISIVO_STRICT_SESSIONS

on in multi-user mode, off otherwise

When on, only session ids minted by the backend are accepted. 0/false/no turns it off, any other non-empty value on.

VISIVO_SESSION_TTL

1800

A session idle for longer than this many seconds is removed and its datasets closed, unless a task of it is still running. The shared anonymous session stays, but its datasets are released.

VISIVO_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_TOKEN

32

Live sessions one token may hold; a further session answers HTTP 429.

VISIVO_TASK_TTL_SECONDS

1800

A task record neither read nor updated for this many seconds is dropped from the task registry (at least 1), after which its status can no longer be polled. Running tasks are never dropped.

VISIVO_SNAPSHOT_SECRET

ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, else random per process

Secret. HMAC key that signs reproducibility snapshots. Set it so signatures stay valid across restarts.

Files and caches¶

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_EXPORTS_DIR

~/.visivo/exports

The Workspace exports folder: saved cut-outs, moment FITS files and source-finding products. Created if missing.

VISIVO_HIPS_CACHE

~/.cache/visivo/hips

Directory of the HiPS tile cache.

VISIVO_HIPS_CACHE_MAX_BYTES

2 GiB

Size cap of the HiPS cache; the least recently used tiles are evicted beyond it.

VISIVO_HIPS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS

604800 (7 days)

Tiles older than this are deleted.

VISIVO_HIPS_CACHE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL

60

Minimum seconds between two cleanup passes over the HiPS cache.

VISIVO_SAMP_FILE_TTL

3600

Files staged for SAMP (in the system temporary directory, visivo_samp_files) are deleted after this many seconds.

Copilot¶

The copilot’s provider is chosen per session in the client; these variables give every new session its starting configuration. See Self-hosted copilot LLM and Copilot backend.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_ASSISTANT_PROVIDER

auto

auto, anthropic, openai or null. auto picks a self-hosted endpoint or OpenAI key first, then an Anthropic key, else null (tools only, no language model).

VISIVO_ASSISTANT_MODEL

provider default

Model name sent to the provider. Without it the Anthropic provider uses claude-opus-4-8 and the OpenAI provider, cloud or self-hosted, uses gpt-4o; a self-hosted server usually needs its own served name here.

VISIVO_LLM_BASE_URL

unset

Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible server (for example http://host:8000/v1). Keep credentials out of it; the key belongs in VISIVO_LLM_API_KEY. A URL set from the client must be http/https with no credentials, query or fragment.

VISIVO_LLM_API_KEY

unset

Secret. Key sent to VISIVO_LLM_BASE_URL, and only there.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

unset

Secret. Key for the Anthropic provider.

OPENAI_API_KEY

unset

Secret. Key for the cloud OpenAI provider; never sent to a self-hosted URL.

VISIVO_ASSISTANT_SLOTS

2

Copilot queries running at once, across all sessions (at least 1). Separate from the heavy-task slots.

VISIVO_ASSISTANT_TIMEOUT_S

120

Wall-clock budget of one copilot query, tool calls included; beyond it the request answers HTTP 504.

Remote services: VLKB, HiPS, cone search, open URL, SAMP¶

Every URL the backend fetches on a client’s behalf is checked against an allowlist variable, separately for each service. When an allowlist is set, only the hosts it names (comma-separated, matched case-insensitively) are fetched and every other host is refused. When it is unset, only http and https URLs are accepted and, except for the open-URL route, addresses that resolve to private, loopback, link-local, reserved or multicast networks are refused. Redirects are checked with the same policy.

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_VLKB_URL

https://vlkb.ia2.inaf.it/vlkb for TAP queries; none for multi-cutout

Default VLKB service when the client sends none.

VISIVO_VLKB_ALLOWED_HOSTS

unset

Allowlist for VLKB TAP, cut-out, multi-cutout and SED-fit requests.

VISIVO_VLKB_MAX_BYTES

8 GiB

Largest single cut-out download.

VISIVO_VLKB_MCUTOUT_TIMEOUT

300

Socket timeout of each multi-cutout archive call.

VISIVO_VLKB_MCUTOUT_MAX_ITEMS

500

Datasets in one multi-cutout batch.

VISIVO_VLKB_MCUTOUT_MAX_BYTES

16 GiB

Largest multi-cutout results archive.

VISIVO_VLKB_MCUTOUT_MAX_EXTRACTED

32 GiB

Total unpacked size of that archive.

VISIVO_VLKB_MCUTOUT_MAX_MEMBERS

2000

Entries in that archive.

VISIVO_VLKB_MCUTOUT_MAX_REPORT

8 MiB

Largest job report.

VISIVO_VLKB_SEDFIT_URL

unset

Base URL of the VLKB SED-fit model service.

VISIVO_SED_MODELS_TIMEOUT

300

Deadline of a whole SED model-fit request.

VISIVO_SED_MODELS_MAX_BYTES

64 MiB

Largest response accepted from the SED-fit service.

VISIVO_SED_MAX_MODELS

2000

Upper bound on the max_models a client may request.

VISIVO_HIPS2FITS_URL

https://alasky.cds.unistra.fr/hips-image-services/hips2fits

hips2fits service, for a mirror.

VISIVO_HIPS2FITS_ALLOWED_HOSTS

unset

Allowlist for hips2fits requests.

VISIVO_CONE_SEARCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS

unset

Allowlist for cone-search requests.

VISIVO_OPENURL_ALLOWED_HOSTS

unset

Allowlist for /v1/datasets/open_url (opening a dataset by URL, as SKAVA access URLs do).

VISIVO_OPENURL_BLOCK_PRIVATE

off

1/true/yes refuses private and loopback addresses on the open-URL route too. Off by default because federated data nodes often sit on private networks.

VISIVO_SAMP_DIRECT

0

1 lets the backend register with a SAMP hub on its own machine and send messages directly. Without it, SAMP goes through the desktop client, which is the only way when the backend is remote.

Analysis limits¶

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_LINEWIDTH_SNR

3.0

Pixels below this signal-to-noise ratio are skipped by the line-width fit; 0 fits every pixel.

VISIVO_LINEWIDTH_CHUNKS

VISIVO_WORKERS

Row chunks a line-width map is split into; the chunks still pass the heavy-task throttle.

VISIVO_KINEMATIC_MAX_VOXELS

268435456 (256 Mi voxels)

Largest kinematic model cube; larger requests answer HTTP 413. Zero or invalid values use the default.

VISIVO_AREPO_MAX_CELLS

600000000

Largest grid an AREPO extraction may materialise.

VISIVO_AREPO_MAX_LEVEL

14

Highest AREPO refinement level accepted.

VISIVO_SOFIA_BIN

sofia2, else sofia, on PATH

The SoFiA-2 executable.

VISIVO_SOFIA_TIMEOUT_S

900

Wall-clock limit of a SoFiA-2 run started from POST /v1/sourcefind/{dataset_id}; 0 disables it.

VISIVO_FINDER_TIMEOUT_S

3600

Wall-clock limit of a source finder run as a task (POST /v1/tasks/sourcefind); at least 1.

Velocity fields¶

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_VELOCITY_STREAM_BYTES

512 MiB

Above this field size, the full-resolution divergence is computed in z-slabs read from disk instead of in memory. 0 always streams.

VISIVO_VELOCITY_SLAB

32

z-planes per slab on the streamed path (at least 1).

Diagnostics¶

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_DIAGNOSTICS_LEVEL

INFO

Lowest Python logging level copied into the diagnostics buffer that View → Diagnostics shows (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR). An unknown name means INFO.

VISIVO_DIAGNOSTICS_BUFFER

2000

Log records kept in that buffer (at least 16); older ones are dropped.

Other variables the backend honours¶

Variable

Effect

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES

The GPUs the job was given. Workers are spread over them (see VISIVO_GPU_ROUND_ROBIN), and so are remote render views.

VTK_EGL_DEVICE_INDEX

Binds every remote render view to this EGL device instead of spreading views over the job’s GPUs.

SLURM_JOB_ID

Marks the backend as running in a SLURM job, so the memory grant below is taken into account.

SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE

Memory granted to the job, in MiB; counts as a memory limit. 0 (the whole node) sets none.

SLURM_MEM_PER_CPU, SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE

Used together as the memory grant when SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE is absent.

ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET

Secret. Fallback for VISIVO_SNAPSHOT_SECRET.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY

See Copilot.
